evidence.title: OpenChamber: Use it where you work; Quick start
evidence.locator: Use it where you work; Quick start
evidence.finding: OpenChamber has macOS, Windows and Linux desktop clients, a web/PWA client, VS Code extension and a CLI/server. Desktop bundles a matching OpenCode CLI; web/VS Code use an installed OpenCode CLI.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Install the app; PWA
evidence.finding: Native iOS uses TestFlight beta and Android is a Canary APK. Phone apps can view sessions, reply and manage work; Safari/Chrome phone browsers can install the PWA. These clients connect to the user server.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Why OpenCode?
evidence.finding: The core workspace uses OpenCode to run coding agents. Model/provider selection through OpenCode does not establish another named harness by itself.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Claude Code
evidence.finding: The optional Claude Code integration uses the official Claude Agent SDK with the installed Claude Code CLI and supported sign-in. This is distinct from ordinary OpenCode provider configuration.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Claude Code
evidence.finding: The Claude Code integration reuses Claude Pro or Max through the local Claude Code CLI sign-in without API keys. Setup can install the CLI and sign in.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Connect a provider; Where sign-ins live
evidence.locator: Connect a provider; Where sign-ins live
evidence.finding: OpenCode stores provider API keys and device-flow sign-ins. Custom OpenAI-compatible providers are configurable; signing into a model provider is separate from a native agent subscription.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Quick start
evidence.finding: Desktop bundles OpenCode; CLI/Web requires Node.js 24.14+ and an installed OpenCode. Users start a local server protected with a UI password before connecting devices.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: CLI for Web and PWA
evidence.finding: Product CLI commands expose status, connect QR links, tunnels, startup control, logs, stop and update. A stable public session API was not inferred merely from the internal web app.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Add a server; Where it applies
evidence.locator: Add a server; Where it applies
evidence.finding: Users configure local command or remote URL MCP servers with headers/environment settings, scoped personally or per project. Servers can be disabled without deletion.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Extensions
evidence.finding: Extensions can add git hosts, trackers, tools, UI and notification destinations. Local services require explicit permission in extension settings.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Start work from an issue or pull request
evidence.locator: Start work from an issue or pull request
evidence.finding: Git host issues and PRs become context for a new worktree/session; the message is not sent automatically. Supported hosts include GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo and Gerrit changes.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Plans; Agents
evidence.finding: Plans are editable Markdown files retained at project level, imported from text/Markdown and optionally moved into the repository. Agents update checklist steps, and the UI shows progress from the Steps section.

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Agents

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Cost and caching

evidence.title: OpenChamber: Agents
